data: Only spacecraft to fly over the Sun's poles — joint ESA / NASA, 1990-2009

Joint ESA + NASA solar / heliospheric mission, built by Dornier with US scientific contribution. Launched 1990-10-06 from STS-41 Discovery + IUS + PAM-S on a high-energy trajectory direct to Jupiter — the only way to fling a spacecraft out of the ecliptic plane without prohibitive delta-v. Jupiter flyby 1992-02-08 deflected the spacecraft into an 80°-inclination heliocentric orbit (1.3 × 5.4 AU, 6.2-year period) — the first and still only spacecraft ever to fly over the Sun's poles. Three pairs of polar passes (approximately 2.5 solar orbits) gave us the heliospheric current sheet 3D structure, the solar wind's faster polar streams + slower equatorial belt, in-situ cosmic-ray latitudinal gradients, and the only multi-decade record of polar coronal hole behaviour over a complete solar cycle. Mission ended 2009-06-30 when the X-band transmitter heater failed.
Smith (2011) — Ulysses heliospheric legacy (Annual Review of Astronomy & Astrophysics 49)
First spacecraft to observe the Sun's poles from above + below the ecliptic — Jupiter gravity assist 1992

Joint ESA + NASA solar / heliospheric mission, built by Dornier with US scientific contribution. Launched 1990-10-06 from STS-41 Discovery on a high-energy trajectory direct to Jupiter — the only way to fling a spacecraft out of the ecliptic plane without prohibitive delta-v. Jupiter flyby 1992-02-08 deflected the spacecraft into an 80°-inclination heliocentric orbit (1.3 × 5.4 AU, 6.2-year period) — the first and still only spacecraft to fly over the Sun's poles. Three complete polar orbits gave us the heliospheric current sheet 3D structure, the faster polar / slower equatorial solar wind, and the only multi-decade record of polar coronal hole behaviour over a complete solar cycle. Mission ended 2009.
Only spacecraft ever to enter a high-inclination heliocentric orbit; only direct measurements of the solar wind at all heliographic latitudes
First detailed imaging of the Sun's polar regions
First Jupiter orbiter; 8 years of measurements
Last Soviet planetary mission; lost at Phobos approach
